data.title: bn-20l: publish first oracle guide against its code
data.description: For bn-20l: adds the checked web.private-object-read.v1 guide, exact check/reason drift tests, and record show guide/limitations projection. Exact review range: base 3620b328882ff70c42a7d84066ec590f61d2fc14, target b994b7f0c903ee56ec77771ba3820da69c27af5b, binary patch SHA-256 7b09b11acb6c7580d61640a351876cc65b80e678e2b2e108a198a93867d44c72. Focused contract and read-process tests pass; RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 just check passes after rebase; strict clippy and just fixture-check pass. Please review the exact range and verify guide scope, digest-bound read projection, and record-applicable limitation handling.

data.body: [risk:medium] Preserve show for legitimate pre-v12 linked records. This lookup makes publication_candidates mandatory for every verification, but migration 012 explicitly sets candidate_required=0 for legacy intents and reconstructs only artifact_id, not record_bytes (012_publication.sql:6-28); migration_v12_reconstructs_completed_intent_artifact_receipts proves that completed rows survive in exactly that shape (store/tests.rs:2157-2248). After migration, show V-legacy now returns INTEGRITY_FAILURE instead of the previously available index metadata; on an unmigrated v11 read-only store the table lookup itself also fails. This conflicts with the historical-record/old-version compatibility contract. Distinguish legitimate candidate_required=0/schema<12 records from missing required staging: preserve their index-only show (and explicitly omit unavailable guide/limitations), or obtain the exact record through an authenticated retained-artifact read path. Keep the current digest/canonical/identity checks and fail closed for candidate_required=1 bytes that are absent or tampered.

[risk:low] Keep title-depth text output title-only. These guide and known-miss rows are emitted even after the title branch at lines 480-482, so scourge show V-... --depth title now expands from one identity row to the guide plus every limitation. That defeats the advertised detail level and can break bounded agent-oriented output. Gate these rows on !title and add exact text assertions for record title/summary/full; the current test exercises only the default summary and substring-matches the additions.

data.body: Fixed: show now preserves index-only records on schema versions before 12 and on migrated v12 intents with candidate_required=0, omitting unavailable guide/limitations. It requires staged bytes only for candidate_required=1 and retains digest, canonical decode, and identity checks; required missing or tampered bytes fail with INTEGRITY_FAILURE. Regressions cover a read before v12 migration, fallback after migration, and required staged-byte deletion/digest tampering.

Fixed: title depth omits guide and limitation fields from JSON and gates the human detail rows, preserving the title-only output. Exact read-process assertions now cover title, summary, and full text plus title/full JSON.

data.body: [risk:medium] Do not let mutable schema/intent flags downgrade a required staged record to a successful legacy view. The new historical_record_show_fallback test seeds a current v12 record (candidate_required=1 with staged bytes) and changes only PRAGMA user_version to 11; this branch then returns success without consulting the candidate at all. Combining that unguarded header change with candidate deletion/corruption masks exactly the required-stage tampering that staged_record_integrity is meant to reject. Likewise, after dropping publication_intent_transition, changing candidate_required to 0 and deleting the candidate reaches the same success path. A legitimate v11 database has no v12 candidate table/column, while a legitimately migrated legacy intent has auditable pre-migration provenance. Require a schema/provenance-consistent legacy state instead of trusting user_version or candidate_required alone; reject a v11 header paired with v12 objects and add regressions for version downgrade + missing/corrupt bytes and required-flag downgrade + candidate deletion.

data.reason: Blocking: mutable user_version/candidate_required can downgrade a current required staged record into the legacy index-only success path, masking missing or corrupted record bytes. Prior depth and genuine legacy compatibility fixes otherwise validate.

data.body: Fixed: legacy fallback now requires matching pre-v12 physical schema and header with no v12 migration receipt, or a candidate_required=0 intent whose publication.intent audit revision predates schema.migrate 12. Current v12 header downgrade and required-flag downgrade with candidate deletion both fail integrity; regressions cover both, while genuine v11 and migrated legacy fallback remain covered.

data.reason: Closed by requiring schema-consistent, audit-backed legacy provenance and adding downgrade regressions.

data.body: Verified at 47695c7564fc45f74d0f1c1c31a0bf9c3e183420: a lowered user_version is rejected when either v12 publication object or its schema.migrate 12 receipt remains; candidate_required=0 is accepted only with no staged row and a publication.intent revision strictly before the migration-12 receipt. The current-record header/flag downgrade tamper cases fail closed, while the genuine physical v11 read and migrated legacy index-only read pass. Focused migration/read/contract tests and strict clippy pass.

data.body: [risk:medium] Bind the guide and registered known-miss projection to the exact oracle contract digest, not ID/version alone. Scope::record verifies only the outer record digest, then drops record.oracle.digest and returns arbitrary record limitations; this branch attaches the current web.private-object-read.v1 guide whenever ID/version match. The checked read-process fixture demonstrates the gap: fixtures/contracts/scourge-v1/verification-record.json carries oracle.digest=dddd... rather than the frozen registry digest 6204d155..., yet the final test expects the current guide and labels its supplied limitation as a known miss. A canonical, outer-digest-consistent staged record from an unqualified or downgraded oracle contract can therefore be presented as governed by the shipped guide. Preserve the oracle digest in RecordView; require exact ID/version/digest provenance before projecting this guide; and validate that projected known misses are the exact applicable registered subset (reject unknowns/duplicates or fail closed). Add a regression that changes the oracle digest/limitations while recomputing the staged outer digest and coordination reference, so the provenance check—not merely the outer checksum—rejects the downgrade. Genuine index-only legacy records should continue omitting guide/limitations, and title/summary should remain bounded.

The reader drops record.oracle.digest and the CLI attaches the current guide on ID/version alone; the shipped read fixture uses a non-frozen dddd... oracle digest yet receives the 6204d155... guide and registered-known-miss labeling. Exact oracle digest and limitation-set provenance must fail closed independently of the outer record checksum. All four supplied validation hashes match and independent contract tests pass 13/13, but those tests do not close this staged-record projection gap. The pinned Teapot refusal remains a disclosed no-traffic qualification limit, not the reason for BLOCK.
